name: Jaipur
shortDesc: The Royal Pink City — Cradle of Block Prints, Blue Pottery & Rajput Lore
historyStory: In 1727 AD, Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II envisioned a city designed according to Shilpa Shastra — ancient Vedic principles of architecture. Wrapped in rose-pink terracotta plaster symbolizing hospitality, Jaipur became a sanctuary for master craftsmen, astronomers, and weavers fleeing chaotic empires. The city's grid layout, nine blocks representing the nine treasure divisions of the universe, preserves living heritage where ancient brass hammer clicks still echo through ancestral havelis.

placesToVisit.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
placesToVisit.desc: A 5-story honeycomb facade crafted with 953 delicate lattice jharokhas for royal women to observe street processions without being seen.

placesToVisit.name: Amber Fort & Palace
placesToVisit.desc: Perched atop Cheel ka Teela (Hill of Eagles), featuring the legendary Sheesh Mahal adorned with thousands of hand-cut convex mirrors.

placesToVisit.name: Jantar Mantar Observatory
placesToVisit.desc: UNESCO World Heritage site housing 19 architectural astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial.

crafts.name: Jaipur Blue Pottery
crafts.desc: Turquoise quartz-based pottery fired without clay, decorated with intricate Persian floral motifs.
crafts.story: Derived from Turko-Persian origins, Turko-Persian artisans migrated to Jaipur under Maharaja Ram Singh II. Unlike standard pottery, it uses ground quartz stone, glass, and natural copper oxide dyes.

crafts.name: Bagru & Sanganeri Block Print
crafts.desc: Hand-carved teakwood blocks dipped in natural vegetable indigo and madder dyes stamped onto unbleached cotton.
crafts.story: Practiced for over 400 years by the Chippa community along the Sanjaria River, relying on sun-baked riverbeds for color fixation.

festivals.name: Teej Festival
festivals.desc: Celebrating Goddess Parvati's union with Lord Shiva with grand palanquin processions, swings in royal gardens, and traditional ghevar sweets.

festivals.name: Jaipur Literature & Heritage Mela
festivals.desc: Gathering of world authors, folk musicians, puppet masters, and traditional artisans at Diggi Palace.

food.name: Dal Baati Churma
food.desc: Baked whole-wheat dough balls dipped in pure desi ghee, served with five-lentil curry and sweet crushed wheat churma.
food.story: Created by warrior Marwari soldiers who buried dough balls in desert sand under sun heat before riding to battle.

food.name: Pyaaz Kachori & Ghevar
food.desc: Flaky deep-fried pastry filled with spiced onions served with disc-shaped honeycombed dessert soaked in saffron syrup.

artisans.name: Master Kirpal Singh Shekhawat Studio
artisans.bio: National Awardee 4th generation artisan family keeping the quartz-pottery glaze legacy alive.

artisans.name: Ramprasad Chippa
artisans.bio: Woodblock carver and natural dye master preserving 200-year-old wooden blocks.

name: Varanasi (Kashi)
shortDesc: The Eternal City — Sacred Ghats, Banarasi Zari Silk & Classical Ragas
historyStory: Older than history, older than tradition, Varanasi sits on the sacred crescent bend of the River Ganges. Mentioned in the Rigveda, Kashi has been the spiritual heartland of India for 3,000 years. It is where Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath, where Tulsidas composed the Ramcharitmanas, and where master Muslim and Hindu weavers forged the world's most intricate silk brocades using gold and silver threads (Zari).

placesToVisit.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
placesToVisit.desc: The primary ghat renowned for the grand evening Ganga Aarti performed with massive brass lamps, incense, and Vedic chants.

placesToVisit.name: Sarnath Deer Park & Stupa
placesToVisit.desc: Where Gautama Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths. Houses the Ashoka Pillar with four lions emblem.

placesToVisit.name: Kashi Vishwanath Corridor
placesToVisit.desc: Historic Jyotirlinga temple connecting ancient stone architecture directly with the ghats of the Holy Ganga.

crafts.name: Banarasi Silk Brocade
crafts.desc: Heavy silk sarees handwoven on pit looms featuring gold silver brocades (Kinkhab), floral motifs (Jaal), and foliage.
crafts.story: Brought to prominence during Mughal emperor Akbar's reign, blending Persian floral aesthetics with traditional Indian motifs.

crafts.name: Varanasi Wooden Lacquerware Toys
crafts.desc: Hand-turned wooden toys coated with natural non-toxic lacquer extracted from tree resins.
crafts.story: Practiced by the ancestral craft communities along the narrow alleyways of Khojwa.

festivals.name: Dev Deepawali
festivals.desc: Over one million earthenware oil lamps (diyas) illuminate every single step of the 84 ghats along the Ganges.

food.name: Banarasi Paan & Malaiyyo
food.desc: Foamy milk dessert infused with saffron, pistachio, and cardamom served in clay pots alongside betel leaf paan.
food.story: Malaiyyo is a winter miracle dessert made by leaving sweetened milk in open air overnight for dew drops to foam it.

artisans.name: Ustad Mukhtar Ansari & Family
artisans.bio: 5th generation Master Weaver operating traditional wooden handlooms in Madanpura.

name: Srinagar
shortDesc: Paradise on Earth — Dal Lake Shikaras, Fine Pashmina & Papier-Mâché Art
historyStory: Founded by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC, Srinagar sits cradled in the Kashmir valley along the Jhelum river. Famed for Mughal gardens laid out by Shah Jahan, Kashmir served as the silk route hub connecting Central Asia with India. The Persian king Zain-ul-Abidin invited artisans from Samarkand, giving birth to Pashmina weaving, carpet knotting, and walnut wood carving.

placesToVisit.name: Dal Lake & Floating Market
placesToVisit.desc: Iconic body of water filled with carved wooden houseboats and floating vegetable markets navigated by Shikaras.

placesToVisit.name: Shalimar Bagh & Nishat Bagh
placesToVisit.desc: Terraced Mughal gardens built in 1619 with cascading fountains and centuries-old Chinar trees.

crafts.name: Kashmiri Hand-Embroidered Pashmina
crafts.desc: Ultra-soft cashmere fleece spun from Changthangi goats, embroidered with needle Sozni floral motifs.
crafts.story: Each shawl takes between 6 months to 2 years of meticulous single-needle hand stitching.

crafts.name: Kashmiri Papier-Mâché
crafts.desc: Paper pulp moulded into boxes, vases, and trays, hand-painted with gold leaf and miniature bird art.
crafts.story: Introduced by Sufi saint Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani from Persia in the 14th century.

festivals.name: Tulip Festival
festivals.desc: Asia's largest tulip garden blossoms with millions of tulips of over 60 varieties against the Zabarwan range.

food.name: Wazwan & Kahwa Tea
food.desc: Traditional 36-course royal meal served on copper platters (Trami) accompanied by green tea infused with saffron and almonds.
food.story: Wazwan cooking is an artform passed down exclusively among hereditary master cooks (Wazas).

artisans.name: Ghulam Nabi & Sons
artisans.bio: Heritable artisan workshop located in Downtown Srinagar.

name: Madurai
shortDesc: The Temple City — Meenakshi Temple Towers, Sungudi Cotton & Jasmine Fragrance
historyStory: Known as the Athens of the East, Madurai has been continuously inhabited for over 2,500 years. Governed by the ancient Sangam Pandyan dynasty, Madurai was the capital where Tamil literature flourished. Centered around the majestic Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple with its 14 soaring gopurams encrusted with thousands of painted deities, it is famous for tie-and-dye Sungudi sarees brought by Saurashtrian weavers centuries ago.

placesToVisit.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
placesToVisit.desc: Architectural wonder featuring 14 gopuram towers, the Hall of 1000 Pillars, and sacred Golden Lotus Tank.

placesToVisit.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
placesToVisit.desc: 17th-century palace built by King Thirumalai Nayak blending Dravidian, Islamic, and Italian Renaissance styles.

crafts.name: Madurai Sungudi Saree
crafts.desc: Traditional cotton saree created using micro tie-and-dye ring dots inspired by cosmic night stars.
crafts.story: Crafted by Saurashtrian migrants who settled under Nayak royal patronage, using natural indigo and alizarin dyes.

festivals.name: Chithirai Festival
festivals.desc: Re-enactment of the divine wedding of Goddess Meenakshi with Lord Sundareswarar drawn on golden chariots.

food.name: Jigarthanda & Madurai Bun Parotta
food.desc: Cooling beverage made with tree gum, nannari syrup, and ice cream alongside multi-layered fluffy bun parotta.
food.story: Jigarthanda literally means 'Heart Cooler', introduced as a refreshing elixir for southern summers.

artisans.name: S. K. Ramanathan Weaver Collective
artisans.bio: Master tie-dye artisan practicing ring-dot technique for over 4 decades.

name: Rann of Kutch
shortDesc: The White Desert — Mirror Embroidery, Ajrakh Print & Salt Marshes
historyStory: Extending to the Arabian Sea, Kutch is a cradle of resilient desert civilizations dating back to Dholavira of the Indus Valley. Communities like the Rabaris, Mutwas, and Meghwals developed intricate mirrorwork embroidery (Abhla Bharat) so women could reflect sunlight and ward off desert evil spirits.

placesToVisit.name: Great Rann White Salt Desert
placesToVisit.desc: Surreal salt marsh landscape shining silvery white under full moon light.

placesToVisit.name: Dhamadka & Ajrakhpur Craft Village
placesToVisit.desc: Dedicated artisan village where 16-stage block printing using mud resist and natural indigo takes place.

crafts.name: Kutchi Mirrorwork & Rabari Embroidery
crafts.desc: Hand-stitched geometric patterns studded with tiny mirrors, silk thread tassels, and chain stitching.
crafts.story: Each nomadic tribe possesses a distinct stitch signature passed from mother to daughter as dowry heirlooms.

crafts.name: Ajrakh Block Printing
crafts.desc: Complex double-sided block printing featuring geometric star grids printed using pomegranate skin, iron, and indigo.
crafts.story: Dating back 4,000 years to Sindhu valley civilization.

festivals.name: Rann Utsav
festivals.desc: Cultural carnival of Gujarati folk dance (Garba, Raas), desert camping, and handicraft fairs.

food.name: Kutchi Dabeli & Bajra No Rotlo
food.desc: Spiced potato burger garnished with pomegranate seeds, roasted peanuts, and served with millet flatbread.
food.story: Invented in Mandvi in 1960 by Keshavji Gabha Chhudasma.

artisans.name: Dr. Ismail Khatri Ajrakh Studio
artisans.bio: Master craftsman awarded honorary doctorate for preserving natural dye chemistry.

name: Bodh Gaya
shortDesc: Land of Enlightenment — Mahabodhi Tree, Madhubani Art & Ancient Wisdom
historyStory: Under the shade of the sacred Peepal tree at Bodh Gaya, Siddhartha Gautama attained Supreme Enlightenment 2,500 years ago, becoming the Buddha. Located in Bihar — the ancient land of Magadha, Nalanda University, and Emperor Ashoka — it is a universal beacon of peace. Nearby Mithila region is home to Madhubani painting, traditionally painted on mud walls by women using twigs and natural pigment paste.

placesToVisit.name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex
placesToVisit.desc: UNESCO World Heritage 50-meter grand pyramidal temple housing the sacred Vajrasana (Diamond Throne) and Bodhi Tree descendant.

placesToVisit.name: Great Buddha Statue
placesToVisit.desc: 25-meter tall stone statue depicting Lord Buddha in meditation pose, unveiled by the Dalai Lama.

crafts.name: Mithila / Madhubani Painting
crafts.desc: Intricate line art drawn with bamboo twigs depicting Hindu deities, peacocks, flora, and geometric borders.
crafts.story: Originated when King Janaka commissioned artists to paint the town of Mithila for Sita's royal wedding to Rama.

festivals.name: Buddha Jayanti / Purnima
festivals.desc: International gathering of Buddhist monks, candle light vigils, and sutra chanting around the sacred Bodhi Tree.

food.name: Litti Chokha & Khaja
food.desc: Whole-wheat dough balls stuffed with roasted gram flour (sattu) cooked over cow dung embers, served with roasted eggplant chokha.
food.story: Litti was the staple food of ancient Mauryan soldiers due to its long shelf-life and nutritional value.

name: Hampi
shortDesc: Forgotten Vijayanagara Empire — Monolithic Stone Chariots & Temples
historyStory: Hampi was the majestic capital of the 14th-century Vijayanagara Empire, described by medieval European travelers as rivaling Rome. Spanning 4,100 hectares along the Tungabhadra River, its boulder-strewn landscape features over 1,600 surviving monuments including stone chariots and musical pillared halls.

placesToVisit.name: Vittala Temple Stone Chariot
placesToVisit.desc: Iconic stone chariot dedicated to Garuda, featuring musical pillars that produce distinct musical notes when tapped.

placesToVisit.name: Virupaksha Temple
placesToVisit.desc: Operating continuously since the 7th century, featuring a 160-foot carved gopuram tower dedicated to Lord Shiva.

crafts.name: Kinhal Wooden Toys
crafts.desc: Soft-wood sculpted idols painted with natural liquid colors by descendants of Vijayanagara empire artisans.
crafts.story: Handcrafted from light Polki wood and coated with resin colors.

festivals.name: Hampi Utsav
festivals.desc: 3-day cultural tribute celebrating Vijayanagara art, drama, and classical music.

food.name: Banana Leaf South Indian Thali
food.desc: Unlimited rice, sambar, rasam, and palya served on fresh banana leaf.
food.story: Authentic temple dining tradition preserved for centuries.

name: Jodhpur
shortDesc: Sun City of Marwar — Mehrangarh Citadel & Bandhani Textiles
historyStory: Founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha, Jodhpur is the historic capital of the Marwar Kingdom. Dominated by the impregnable Mehrangarh Fort perched 400 feet above blue-painted Brahmin houses, it is famed for tie-dye Bandhani textiles, antique rosewood carving, and spicy Marwari street food.

placesToVisit.name: Mehrangarh Fort
placesToVisit.desc: One of India's largest forts built in 1459, featuring colossal stone walls, Sheesh Mahal, and expansive courtyards.

placesToVisit.name: Jaswant Thada
placesToVisit.desc: A royal white marble cenotaph built in 1899, known as the Taj Mahal of Marwar.

crafts.name: Jodhpur Bandhani
crafts.desc: Intricate tie-dye textile art with tiny tied knots creating vibrant sunburst patterns.
crafts.story: Ancient tie-and-dye craft practiced by Marwari textile masters.

festivals.name: Marwar Festival
festivals.desc: Celebration of Langa & Manganiyar folk music bards.

food.name: Pyaaz Kachori & Mirchi Bada
food.desc: Large green chillies stuffed with seasoned potato and deep-fried served hot.
food.story: Iconic street food staple of Marwar.

artisans.name: Marwar Bandhani Collective
artisans.bio: Master craftsmen producing hand-dyed royal textiles.

name: Agra
shortDesc: Mughal Empire Capital — Taj Mahal, Pietra Dura & Marble Inlay
historyStory: Agra was the glorious capital of the Mughal Empire under Shah Jahan, Akbar, and Jahangir. Built along the banks of the Yamuna River, it houses the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Itmad-ud-Daulah. Famed for Pietra Dura marble inlay craft, Zardozi embroidery, and Mughlai cuisine.

placesToVisit.name: Taj Mahal
placesToVisit.desc: UNESCO World Heritage site built by Shah Jahan in white Makrana marble with Pietra Dura gemstones.

placesToVisit.name: Agra Fort
placesToVisit.desc: Massive 94-acre red sandstone fortress housing Diwan-i-Khas, Jahangiri Mahal, and Sheesh Mahal.

placesToVisit.name: Itmad-Ud-Daulah's Tomb
placesToVisit.desc: Known as the 'Baby Taj', the first Mughal monument built entirely of white marble with lattice screens.

crafts.name: Pietra Dura Marble Inlay
crafts.desc: Precision gemstone inlay work in white marble using lapis lazuli, turquoise, and carnelian.
crafts.story: Heritage artisan technique passed down by descendants of Taj Mahal masons.

festivals.name: Taj Mahotsav
festivals.desc: 10-day carnival of Indian arts, crafts, music, and food.

food.name: Agra Petha & Mughlai Bedmi Poori
food.desc: Ash gourd translucent candy and spiced lentil pooris.
food.story: Royal sweet formulated during Taj Mahal construction.

name: Mumbai
shortDesc: Gateway to India — Apollo Bunder Arch, Elephanta Caves & Marine Drive
historyStory: Originally an archipelago of seven islands inhabited by Koli fisherfolk, Mumbai grew into a financial and cultural metropolis. Famed for the Indo-Saracenic Gateway of India, UNESCO Elephanta Island rock-cut cave temples, and Warli tribal art.

placesToVisit.name: Gateway of India
placesToVisit.desc: Iconic 26-meter arch monument built at Apollo Bunder in 1911 in Indo-Saracenic basalt stone style.

placesToVisit.name: Elephanta Caves
placesToVisit.desc: 5th-century rock-cut cave temples on Elephanta Island housing the colossal Trimurti Shiva sculpture.

crafts.name: Warli Tribal Art
crafts.desc: Folk wall paintings drawn with white rice paste.
crafts.story: Indigenous tribal tradition of Maharashtra.

name: Old & New Delhi
shortDesc: Seat of Dynasties — Red Fort Citadel, Qutub Minar & Akshardham
historyStory: Delhi has served as the capital of seven historic empires including the Tomars, Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, and British Raj. Houses iconic heritage landmarks like Red Fort, 73-meter Qutub Minar, and Akshardham.

placesToVisit.name: Red Fort
placesToVisit.desc: Mughal imperial red sandstone citadel built by Shah Jahan in Shahjahanabad.

placesToVisit.name: Qutub Minar
placesToVisit.desc: 73-meter tall red sandstone UNESCO minaret with ancient non-rusting Iron Pillar.

placesToVisit.name: Akshardham Temple
placesToVisit.desc: Colossal carved pink sandstone and white marble mandir complex showcasing Indian heritage.

crafts.name: Zardozi Embroidery
crafts.desc: Metallic thread embroidery.
crafts.story: Mughal court art.

name: Kolkata
shortDesc: Cultural Capital — Victoria Memorial Marble, Howrah Bridge & Terracotta
historyStory: Kolkata was the capital of British India until 1911. Situated along the Hooghly River, it is famed for the white marble Victoria Memorial, iconic cantilever Howrah Bridge, and Durga Puja street carnivals.

placesToVisit.name: Victoria Memorial
placesToVisit.desc: Grand white Makrana marble museum surrounded by 64 acres of lush gardens.

placesToVisit.name: Howrah Bridge
placesToVisit.desc: Iconic 705-meter balanced cantilever steel bridge spanning the Hooghly River.

crafts.name: Kantha Stitch & Terracotta
crafts.desc: Running stitch embroidery and clay sculptures.
crafts.story: Rural Bengal heritage.

festivals.name: Durga Puja
festivals.desc: UNESCO Intangible Heritage street art festival.

name: Amritsar
shortDesc: City of Golden Temple — Harmandir Sahib, Phulkari & Langar Tradition
historyStory: Founded in 1577 by Guru Ram Das Ji around a sacred pool (Amrit Sarovar). The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) is overlaid with over 750 kg of pure gold foil. Operates the world's largest free community kitchen.

placesToVisit.name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
placesToVisit.desc: Sacred gold-plated Sikh shrine surrounded by Amrit Sarovar lake.

placesToVisit.name: Jallianwala Bagh
placesToVisit.desc: Historic national memorial park preserving bullet-marked walls.

crafts.name: Phulkari Embroidery
crafts.desc: Vibrant flower work darn-stitched on coarse khaddar.
crafts.story: Punjabi wedding heirloom.

name: Hyderabad
shortDesc: City of Pearls — Charminar Minarets, Golconda Fort & Lac Bangles
historyStory: Founded in 1591 by Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah along the Musi River. Famed for the 400-year-old Charminar, acoustic miracle of Golconda Fort, pearl markets, and Bidri metal inlay.

placesToVisit.name: Charminar
placesToVisit.desc: 1591 AD square structure with 4 grand arches and 56-meter minarets overlooking Laad Bazaar.

placesToVisit.name: Golconda Fort
placesToVisit.desc: Impregnable citadel famed for acoustic clapping dome signalling warnings 1 km away.

crafts.name: Bidriware Metal Inlay
crafts.desc: Silver wire inlay on zinc-copper alloy.
crafts.story: GI-tagged Qutb Shahi art.

food.name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
food.desc: Basmati rice cooked dum style with saffron.

name: Mysuru
shortDesc: Heritage Palace City — Mysore Royal Palace, Mysore Silk & Rosewood Inlay
historyStory: Capital of the Wodeyar Dynasty from 1399 to 1947. Famous for the illuminated Mysore Palace, Chamundeshwari Temple atop Chamundi Hill, gold leaf painting, and Mysore Silk sarees.

placesToVisit.name: Mysore Palace
placesToVisit.desc: Indo-Saracenic palace illuminated by 97,000 light bulbs during Dasara.

crafts.name: Mysore Rosewood Inlay
crafts.desc: Ivory and wood marquetry.
crafts.story: Royal craft guild.

name: Konark & Puri
shortDesc: Temple Coast — Sun Chariot Temple, Jagannath Temple & Pattachitra Art
historyStory: Located along the Bay of Bengal, Konark features the 13th-century Sun Temple built as a giant 24-wheeled stone chariot. Nearby Puri is home to the sacred Jagannath Temple and Rath Yatra.

placesToVisit.name: Konark Sun Temple
placesToVisit.desc: 1250 AD UNESCO World Heritage stone chariot dedicated to Sun God Surya.

crafts.name: Pattachitra Palm Leaf Painting
crafts.desc: Scroll painting on cloth/palm leaf.
crafts.story: Ancient Odia ritual art.

name: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar
shortDesc: Cave Temple Capital — Ajanta Paintings, Ellora Kailasa & Himroo Textiles
historyStory: Gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave temples of Ajanta (30 Buddhist caves) and Ellora (Kailasa temple carved top-down from a single monolithic granite mountain).

placesToVisit.name: Ajanta Caves
placesToVisit.desc: 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves dating from 2nd century BCE famous for ancient wall murals.

placesToVisit.name: Ellora Caves (Kailasa Temple)
placesToVisit.desc: Monolithic temple Cave 16 carved top-to-bottom out of a single basalt rock cliff.

crafts.name: Himroo Fabric Weaving
crafts.desc: Cotton-silk brocade fabric.
crafts.story: Royal Nizam court textile.

food.name: Naan Qalia & Puran Poli
food.desc: Spiced mutton stew served with naan.
